name: Washington Wizards
notes: The Wizards play at Capital One Arena in Washington, D.C., in the NBA's Eastern Conference Southeast Division. After finishing with the league's worst record in 2025-26, they won the draft lottery and took BYU forward AJ Dybantsa No. 1 overall, then rebuilt the roster around him, Trae Young and Anthony Davis via a wave of 2026 offseason trades. Entering 2026-27, Washington is a team in transition, pairing a deep young core (Sarr, Coulibaly, Carrington, George, Johnson, Riley) with recently added veterans (Young, Davis, Middleton, Ayton) as it tries to accelerate its rebuild.

roster.facts: Washington's No. 1 overall pick in 2026 after averaging 25.5 points per game at BYU; installed as the franchise's long-term cornerstone.
roster.name: AJ Dybantsa

roster.facts: Signed a four-year, $212 million extension in 2026 after a brief trade to Memphis, locking in as Washington's starting point guard and offensive engine.
roster.name: Trae Young

roster.facts: Former eight-time All-Star acquired from Dallas before the 2026 deadline; his health remains the season's biggest swing factor after just 71 games over two years.
roster.name: Anthony Davis

roster.facts: 2024's No. 2 overall pick coming off a strong rookie season (13 ppg, 1.5 blocks) that projects him as the frontcourt's long-term defensive anchor.
roster.name: Alex Sarr

roster.facts: Former No. 1 overall pick acquired from the Lakers in July 2026 for Jaden Hardy, adding a proven starting center to the frontcourt mix.
roster.name: Deandre Ayton

roster.facts: Three-time All-Star back for a second Wizards stint via a six-team, $17.6 million sign-and-trade in July 2026, brought in as a veteran mentor.
roster.name: Khris Middleton

roster.facts: 2023's No. 7 pick broke out in 2025-26 with 11.7 points, 4.3 rebounds and improved two-way play at just 22 years old.
roster.name: Bilal Coulibaly

roster.facts: 2024's No. 24 pick, a versatile 6'8" wing the Wizards are developing as a floor-spacing forward alongside the team's young core.
roster.name: Kyshawn George

roster.facts: Drafted No. 6 overall in 2025 out of Texas, the young scoring guard enters year two as a key piece of Washington's rebuild.
roster.name: Tre Johnson

roster.facts: 2025's No. 21 pick, acquired in a draft-night trade with Utah; became the first Wizards rookie since 1994 with back-to-back 30-point games.
roster.name: Will Riley

roster.facts: 2024's No. 14 pick out of Pittsburgh, a young combo guard the Wizards are grooming to eventually run the offense.
roster.name: Bub Carrington

roster.facts: Acquired from Charlotte in an August 2026 five-team trade that sent Cam Whitmore to Cleveland, adding scoring depth off the bench.
roster.name: Tre Mann

roster.facts: Undrafted find turned reliable rotation forward, averaging 8.7 points and 5.6 rebounds in 2025-26 under a multi-year contract.
roster.name: Justin Champagnie

roster.facts: Serbian stretch big and 2023 second-round pick providing frontcourt depth and outside shooting behind Sarr, Davis and Ayton.
roster.name: Tristan Vukcevic

roster.facts: Florida State product and 2024 second-round pick, a defensive-minded wing fighting for rotation minutes on a crowded roster.
roster.name: Jamir Watkins

roster.facts: Nigerian-born big man drafted No. 46 overall in 2026 out of Tennessee, where he made the SEC All-Defensive Team, signed to a two-way deal.
roster.name: Felix Okpara
